channel.title: ICU Scope
channel.description: Daily-updated ICU/critical-care literature and FOAMed, organized by organ system.

item.title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.

item.title: Mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of pyroptosis in sepsis‑induced acute lung injury (Review).
item.description: This review explores the mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of pyroptosis in sepsis-induced acute lung injury. Pyroptosis is a critical driver of lung injury and inflammation, and its pathways can be targeted for personalized treatments. Researchers have identified biomarkers and potential inhibitors to enable more effective interventions.

item.title: Fluid and Electrolyte Management in Critically Ill Patients with Infections.
item.description: Critically ill patients with infections struggle to maintain fluid balance due to increased capillary permeability and organ dysfunction. Inadequate fluid balance can increase complications, morbidity, and mortality. Skilled nursing and advanced monitoring are essential to optimize outcomes.

item.title: COMPARE-VENT Feasibility Pilot Study
item.description: The COMPARE-VENT Feasibility Pilot Study explored the challenges of cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) admissions, particularly those requiring advanced respiratory support and invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). These patients often have impaired cardiovascular reserve, making them vulnerable to the adverse effects of positive pressure ventilation (PPV) and systemic sedation. The study aimed to assess the feasibility of a new approach to address these challenges.

item.title: A Prospective Observational Study Using the FAM-CAM
item.description: This study observed whether family members can identify signs of delirium in ICU patients that may not be detected by routine screening. Participants received usual medical care. Family members were asked to report any signs of delirium.

item.title: Resuscitative TEE Collaborative Registry
item.description: This study evaluated the clinical impact and safety of focused, point-of-care transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) in critically-ill patients. The study aimed to determine the clinical impact and safety of TEE performed during routine clinical care. No specific findings were reported.

item.title: Diffuse Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS), Recruitment Maneuver, and sRAGE (DAMAGE Study)
item.description: This study investigated the effect of a recruitment maneuver on plasma sRAGE levels in patients with ALI/ARDS. The study found that a recruitment maneuver increased plasma sRAGE levels. The study was a prospective monocentric randomized controlled cross-over study.

item.title: Impact of Metabolite Supplementation to Restore Mitochondrial Dysfunction During Septic Shock: a Preclinical Study
item.description: This preclinical study investigated the impact of exogenous metabolites on restoring mitochondrial function in septic shock patients with lactate acidosis. The study aimed to evaluate the effect of metabolite supplementation on mitochondrial metabolism in septic shock. The results of this study are not reported.

item.title: Fluid Administration and Fluid Accumulation in the Intensive Care Unit
item.description: This study aimed to describe fluid administration and accumulation in ICU patients. It provided contemporary data on fluid accumulation, risk factors, management, and outcomes in critically ill adults. The study did not report any specific findings or results.

item.title: Clinical Performance of 3D-Printed vs. Milled Endocrowns
item.description: This clinical trial compared the durability and functionality of 3D-printed versus milled endocrowns in the oral cavity. The study aimed to investigate the effect of different materials on clinical success. No results were reported.

item.title: Vadadustat for the Treatment of Nonintubated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Due to Pathogen-Associated Lung Injury
item.description: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of vadadustat in treating nonintubated patients with ARDS caused by pathogen-associated lung injury. No results were reported.

item.title: Heterogeneous Treatment Effects of Renal Replacement Therapy in Critically Ill Patients: A Multicenter Observational Study Using a Japanese ICU Registry.
item.description: This study used a large Japanese ICU registry to investigate the effects of renal replacement therapy (RRT) on hospital mortality. While RRT was associated with higher hospital mortality overall, the study found that certain subgroups of patients may benefit from RRT, such as those with elevated serum creatinine, reduced urine output, and elevated blood urea nitrogen levels.

item.title: EMCrit 431 – OB-EMCrit – Life-Threatening Post-Partum Hemorrhage (PPH) with Cho Espinoza
item.description: Dr. Cho Espinosa discusses how to manage life-threatening post-partum hemorrhage with a focus on uterotonic administration, physical compression techniques, and coagulopathy management.

item.title: A Slow Retreat
item.description: The standard of care for post-cardiac arrest management, targeted temperature management (TTM), may be based on a flawed premise. The evidence supporting TTM has been questioned. The foundation of TTM is being reevaluated.

item.title: Diaphragmatic Ultrasonography in Difficult Weaning
item.description: Researchers used ultrasound to assess diaphragmatic and extradiaphragmatic muscles in patients with difficult weaning from mechanical ventilation. They found that diaphragmatic ultrasonography can help determine the readiness of patients for weaning. The study suggests that this method may improve the success rate of weaning.

item.title: Soluble Forms and Ligands of RAGE in ALI/ARDS (SoLiRAGE).
item.description: Researchers studied soluble forms and ligands of RAGE in patients with Acute Lung Injury (ALI) and Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS). They found elevated levels of soluble RAGE in plasma and pulmonary edema fluid from these patients. This may be a novel marker of alveolar epithelial type I cell injury.

item.title: Pulmonary and Ventilatory Effects of Bed Verticalization in Patients With Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
item.description: This study investigated the effects of bed verticalization on patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The study found no reported pulmonary and ventilatory effects of bed verticalization in patients with ARDS. No specific outcomes were reported.

item.title: Blood Culture Collection Strategies for Suspected Bloodstream Infection
item.description: This study compares two blood culture collection strategies in adults with suspected sepsis. The goal is to evaluate their diagnostic performance and potential impact on patient discomfort and contamination risk.

item.title: Early Sepsis Recognition Tool
item.description: Researchers developed an early recognition tool for sepsis in children based on the Phoenix definition. They also investigated how to implement this tool in clinical practice. The study aimed to address the need for evidence-based approaches to identifying sepsis in diverse healthcare settings in Asia.

item.title: The impact of an intensive care telemedicine program on weaning from invasive ventilation: a secondary analysis of the ERIC trial.
item.description: BACKGROUND: ICU patients commonly require invasive mechanical ventilation. Although weaning from ventilation is crucial for patient outcomes, it is commonly not performed according to guideline recommendations. We investigated if a complex telemedicine intervention improves the weaning process and outcomes. item.title: GRAM NEGATIVES STUDY
item.description: This study aimed to develop a predictive model for mortality in critically ill patients with multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria. It also investigated the characteristics of patients who acquire colonization during ICU stay and the infectious complications they develop.

item.title: STimulation to Activate RespIration
item.description: This was a feasibility trial to test the safety and practicality of using diaphragm neurostimulation-assisted ventilation in patients on mechanical ventilation for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure with lung injury.

item.title: Cardiovascular Protection After Preeclampsia With Enalapril
item.description: This study aimed to assess the willingness of postpartum women to be randomized to different blood pressure medications and their effect on blood pressure in women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. However, it did not find any participants willing to be randomized.

item.title: RESTORE-ZG: Return of Effective Spontaneous Circulation Resuscitation Evaluation Canton of Zug
item.description: This study evaluated cardiac arrest care provided by emergency medical services in Switzerland, focusing on factors that influence return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). The study aimed to identify predictors of ROSC in out-of-hospital cardiac arrests. No specific outcomes or effect measures were reported.

item.title: Conservative Oxygen for Unresponsive Patients after Cardiac Arrest.
item.description: BACKGROUND: In patients who are unresponsive after resuscitation from cardiac arrest, limiting oxygen exposure to that necessary to achieve acceptable oxygenation may increase the likelihood of survival with a favorable functional outcome. METHODS: We randomly assigned unresponsive adults receiving mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU) after cardiac arrest to conservative or liberal oxygen therapy. item.title: PulmCrit Wee: Four reasons that hyperangulated videolaryngoscopy should be the mainstay of ICU intubations
item.description: The author advocates for hyperangulated videolaryngoscopy as the primary method for intubating critically ill patients, citing several reasons for this recommendation.

item.title: İntensive Care Sepsis Prevelance in Turkey (INSEP-TURK)
item.description: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of sepsis and septic shock in adult intensive care units in Turkey. However, it appears to be a descriptive study without explicit findings on prevalence or other key statistics.

item.title: Anticipating Decline and Providing Therapy
item.description: This pilot study will test the feasibility of a new intervention called ADAPT, which aims to support older adults after ICU discharge.

item.title: Open-Label Study to Assess Safety and Time to Catheter-related Bloodstream Infections (CRBSI) in Subjects From Birth to < 18 Years of Age
item.description: This study assessed the safety and time to Catheter-related Bloodstream Infections (CRBSI) of DefenCath in pediatric patients on chronic hemodialysis for kidney failure.

item.title: Validation of SOFA-2 for Mortality and Sepsis-3 Prevalence in Turkey
item.description: This study aimed to validate the SOFA-2 score in predicting mortality and determining sepsis prevalence in Turkish ICUs. Researchers compared the new SOFA-2 score to the existing SOFA-1 score. The study's results are not yet reported.

item.title: Low-intensity Versus Medium-intensity Continuous Kidney Replacement Therapy for Critically Ill Patients
item.description: This clinical trial compared the effectiveness and safety of low-intensity versus medium-intensity continuous kidney replacement therapy in critically ill patients.

item.title: Teamwork for Resilient Staff and Safe Care in ICU
item.description: This ethnographic study observed how healthcare professionals work together in an ICU, exploring teamwork practices and challenges, and how they changed during the COVID-19 pandemic.

item.title: Sequential Compression Device in Distributive Peripheral Edema and Hemodynamic Stability Among Patients in Critical Care Units
item.description: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of sequential compression devices on distributive peripheral edema and hemodynamic stability in critical care patients. The study objectives were to assess the effectiveness of the device and explore relationships between its effectiveness, range of motion, and demographic characteristics. No specific outcomes were reported.

item.title: Comparing The Safety And Efficacy Of DEFENCATH® In Reducing Central-Line Bloodstream Infections (CLABSIs) In Adults Receiving Total Parenteral Nutrition Through A Central Venous Catheter (CVC)
item.description: This study compared the safety and efficacy of DefenCath to heparin in reducing central-line bloodstream infections in adults receiving total parenteral nutrition through a central venous catheter.

item.title: Basic Fracture Treatment
item.description: This is a customizable poster for treating fractures in the emergency department, featuring radiographs, splinting guidance, and fillable local follow-up pathways.

item.title: Evaluation of Emergency Medicine Pharmacist Impact on Blood Culture Review Following Emergency Department Discharge
item.description: Emergency Medicine pharmacists reviewed blood cultures from patients discharged from the Emergency Department. They found that timely review of blood cultures by pharmacists improved the speed of notification for true positive cultures. This led to better patient outcomes.

item.title: Correlation of Memory CD8+ T Cells With Sepsis Severity and Mortality: a Single-center, Unblinded, Prospective, Non-interventional, Observational Study
item.description: Researchers investigated the relationship between memory CD8+ T cells and sepsis severity and mortality in a single-center, observational study. They found a correlation between memory CD8+ T cells and sepsis severity and mortality. The study suggests that immune dysfunction plays a key role in organ damage and early death in sepsis patients.

item.title: Epidemiology and Overtime Genomic Evolution of Klebsiella Pneumoniae and Enterobacter Cloacae Complex (ECC) in Stools of ICU's Patients
item.description: This study explores the epidemiology and genomic evolution of Klebsiella Pneumoniae and Enterobacter Cloacae Complex in ICU patients, highlighting the risk of infection and the emergence of multidrug-resistant isolates.

item.title: A Study in Priors Part 2
item.description: This study applied Bayesian analysis concepts to a meta-analysis comparing normal saline with balanced crystalloids in critically ill patients. The BEST-Living meta-analysis found a difference in outcomes between the two fluids. The study aimed to provide a nuanced understanding of the data.

item.title: REBEL MIND – Teaching Towards Expertise with Gamification
item.description: This podcast episode introduces a gamified teaching tool called Rapid Sequence, aimed at improving clinician learning in critical care. The tool is part of a series focusing on productivity, provider performance, and team optimization. No specific study or data is presented.

item.title: Electrical Impedance Tomography-Guided Identification of the Optimal Lateral Position in Postoperative ARDS
item.description: This study used a new imaging technique to find the best position for patients with lung problems after surgery. They compared lying on the left or right side versus lying flat, and found that one position worked better than the others. The best position helped improve how well oxygen was delivered to the lungs.

item.title: Induced Blood-Stage Malaria in Healthy Malaria-Naive Adults to Assess the Safety and Infectivity of Plasmodium Vivax Challenge Agent and Evaluate Transmission in Mosquito Feeding Assays
item.description: Researchers induced blood-stage malaria in healthy adults to study malaria development, immune response, and transmission to mosquitoes. The study aimed to understand how malaria progresses in people and how it spreads to mosquitoes. Participants were healthy individuals aged 18-54 from the Washington DC area.

item.title: Monitoring of Neuromuscular Blockade in the Intensive Care Unit: a Reliability Study
item.description: This study evaluated the reliability of neuromuscular blockade monitoring in adult ICU patients. It aimed to determine if clinicians can accurately detect neuromuscular blockade and if monitoring is safe. The study found that monitoring was reliable and safe.

item.title: Vasopressin for Septic Shock Pragmatic Trial
item.description: This study will evaluate two different strategies for treating septic shock with vasopressors, focusing on when to add vasopressin. The trial aims to determine the optimal threshold for starting vasopressin in septic shock treatment. The study design is a pragmatic, cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover trial.

item.title: Microbial Metabolites and Outcomes of Pregnancy Study
item.description: This study explores the connection between diet, gut microbiota, and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, a leading cause of maternal and neonatal morbidity.

item.title: Intranasal Insulin to Prevent Intensive Care Unit Delirium
item.description: This study explored the potential of intranasal insulin to prevent delirium in elderly ICU patients after complex cardiac surgery. The study aimed to assess the feasibility, tolerability, and efficacy of this treatment. No results were reported.

item.title: Epidural Analgesia for Pancreatitis (Epipan Study)
item.description: The Epipan Study discusses acute pancreatitis (AP) management, noting that 80% of patients develop mild disease and 20% develop severe disease with local complications.

item.title: Burden of and risk factors for neurological complications in critical illness.
item.description: This review examines the burden and risk factors of neurological complications in critical illness, highlighting the need for standardized definitions and surveillance practices. Neurological complications are common and contribute to morbidity, mortality, and long-term disability. The review identifies knowledge gaps and limitations in understanding the mechanisms of neurological injury and recovery.

item.title: Effects of a clinical metagenomics intervention on clinical outcomes, healthcare costs, and health-related quality of life in patients with sepsis or septic shock: results of the randomized-controlled DigiSep trial.

item.title: Determinants of Delayed Recovery of Consciousness After Analgosedation Discontinuation in the ICU: Insights From Patients With COVID-19 Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure.
item.description: Researchers studied 784 critically ill COVID-19 patients to understand why some take longer to regain consciousness after stopping sedation. They found that many patients took longer than expected to recover, and that factors like age, hypoxemia, and acute kidney injury were associated with delayed recovery. Patients who received dexmedetomidine as an adjunct sedative tended to recover more quickly.

item.title: Erratum: AASLD Practice Guidance on Acute-on-chronic liver failure and the management of critically ill patients with cirrhosis.
Enteral When Compared With IV Magnesium Replacement in the Critically Ill: A Noninferiority Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.description: Researchers compared enteral (taken through the gut) and IV (intravenous) magnesium replacement in critically ill patients with mild-to-moderate hypomagnesemia. They found that enteral replacement was not as effective as IV replacement in correcting low magnesium levels, but it reduced waste, costs, and environmental impact. Enteral replacement also decreased urine magnesium concentrations.

item.title: Sodium Bicarbonate for Acute Metabolic Acidosis in Critically Ill Adults: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
item.description: This meta-analysis of 4 trials found that sodium bicarbonate reduced the need for renal replacement therapy in critically ill adults with acute metabolic acidosis, and may also lower mortality, although evidence is still inconclusive.

item.title: Rocuronium dose and first-attempt intubation success in the critically ill: secondary analysis of two multicenter trials.
item.description: Researchers analyzed data from 2 large studies to see if a higher dose of rocuronium helped patients get intubated on the first try in the ICU. They found that a higher dose of rocuronium was associated with a slightly higher chance of successful intubation on the first attempt, especially in the ICU. This difference was not seen in emergency department intubations.
